speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing fever and altered mental status for the past two days; to begin our assessment, have you had any recent travel, insect bites, or known exposure to sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; regarding your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, have you experienced any recent dose changes or missed doses? Additionally, can you describe the specific nature of your altered mental status, such as confusion, disorientation, or lethargy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use. The combination of fever, altered mental status, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is diagnostic. I recommend immediate admission for supportive care and consideration of dantrolene or bromocriptine.
